faq.a: Umar is associated with the Arabic form عُمَر, whose core sense is umar; flourishing, populated.

faq.q: What is the origin of Umar?
faq.a: Umar is associated with Arabic. Umar is Arabic عُمَر (ʿUmar), associated with the sense 'flourishing, populated'. It was borne by the second caliph.
Yes — the underlying form عُمَر is Arabic.
Umar can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Umar should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿUmar is not a Quranic personal name.
